standard_prerequisites.name: Totally ramified separable extensions and the Eisenstein minimal polynomial of a uniformizer
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the presentation B_1 = B[t]/(P(t)) with the uniformizer.

standard_prerequisites.name: Weak unramifiedness implying that the uniformizer is preserved
standard_prerequisites.use: Is what makes the displayed ring a discrete valuation ring over B.

core_obligations: Let pi in A and pi_1 in A_1 be uniformizers; since K_1/K is totally ramified with respect to A one has pi_1^e = u_1 pi for a unit u_1 of A_1 (proof lines 34501-34503).

Conclude that A_1 is generated over A by pi_1 and that the minimal polynomial P(t) of pi_1 over K has the displayed Eisenstein form t^e + a_{e-1} t^{e-1} + ... + a_0 with a_i in (pi) and a_0 = u pi for a unit u of A (proof lines 34504-34509).
Use that A -> B is weakly unramified to conclude that pi is a uniformizer of B (proof lines 34510-34511).
Conclude that B_1 = B[t]/(P(t)) is a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer the class of t, from which the three assertions of the lemma follow (proof lines 34512-34513).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an extension A -> B of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields K in L, assumes A -> B weakly unramified, and asserts that for any finite separable extension K_1/K totally ramified with respect to A one has that L_1 = L tensor_K K_1 is a field, that A_1 and B_1 = B tensor_A A_1 are discrete valuation rings, and that the extension A_1 in B_1 is weakly unramified (source lines 34489-34498). The proof works with uniformizers and the minimal polynomial. Writing pi in A and pi_1 in A_1 for uniformizers, total ramifiedness gives pi_1^e = u_1 pi for a unit u_1 of A_1, so that A_1 is generated over A by pi_1 and the minimal polynomial P(t) of pi_1 over K has the displayed Eisenstein shape t^e + a_{e-1} t^{e-1} + ... + a_0 with all a_i in (pi) and a_0 = u pi for a unit u of A (proof lines 34501-34509). The proof records that e = [K_1 : K] (proof line 34510). The substantive step is the base change: since A -> B is weakly unramified, pi is a uniformizer of B, so B_1 = B[t]/(P(t)) is a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer the class of t, from which all three assertions follow (proof lines 34510-34513). The non-routine content is the reduction of the weak unramifiedness of the base change to the statement that B[t]/(P(t)) is a discrete valuation ring with the evident uniformizer.
